title: Scheduler: instrument queue depth + effective tokens/sec; add prefill/decode tracing spans
author: Sofia Ivanova
release_notes: Adds scheduler-level metrics for queueing/saturation and tracing spans for prefill/decode to support Dedicated throughput SLO dashboards and triage.
description: Context: As part of the Dedicated throughput SLO work, we need first-class signals that explain when throughput drops due to queueing/scheduler saturation vs model/runtime regressions. Today we have request-level latency and gateway throughput, but we can’t easily answer: (a) are requests waiting in the scheduler queue, (b) how much time is spent in prefill vs decode, and (c) what is the scheduler’s effective token production rate under real traffic. This PR adds low-cardinality scheduler metrics and OTEL tracing spans that can be correlated with deployment/tier/model and used to build alertable panels. What’s included: 1) Scheduler metrics (Prometheus): - redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth (gauge): current queue depth in the scheduler (requests waiting to be scheduled). - redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_ms (histogram): time from enqueue -> scheduling start. - redwood_runtime_scheduler_active_requests (gauge): requests currently owned by scheduler (in-flight). - redwood_runtime_scheduler_batch_size (histogram): effective batch sizes observed at dispatch. - redwood_runtime_effective_output_tokens_total (counter): output tokens emitted by the runtime (decode phase), incremented at the scheduler boundary. - redwood_runtime_effective_output_tokens_per_second (gauge): computed as rate(output_tokens_total) over a rolling window inside the process to avoid query-time pitfalls and keep dashboards consistent. 2) Tracing (OpenTelemetry): Adds spans around runtime phases with stable attributes: - span "scheduler.enqueue" (attributes: deployment_id, model, tier, region, route) - span "scheduler.dispatch" (attributes: batch_size, queue_depth_at_dispatch) - span "runtime.prefill" (attributes: prompt_tokens, max_new_tokens) - span "runtime.decode" (attributes: output_tokens) Notes: request_id is attached as a trace attribute only (not a metric label) to avoid cardinality blow-ups. 3) Naming/labels: Metrics follow the Dedicated metrics taxonomy conventions (deployment_id, tier, region, model) with guardrails: model is normalized (catalog slug), and deployment_id can be disabled via config for shared/internal clusters. 4) Tests + overhead: Adds unit tests for metric emission and a micro-benchmark asserting <0.5% overhead at 1k req/s on synthetic scheduler loop (measured on CI perf runner; see notes below). Motivation for “effective tokens/sec”: We want a metric that tracks the scheduler-visible token output rate without coupling to gateway sampling artifacts. The new gauge uses a rolling EWMA over 30s (configurable) to produce a stable value for dashboards and alerting; Prometheus counters are still exported for raw rate queries. Rollout plan: - Default enabled for Dedicated clusters once dashboards are ready (ENG-2201), but gated behind runtime flag RUNTIME_SCHEDULER_OBS_V1 for staged rollout. - For Hosted/shared, deployment_id labeling defaults off unless explicitly enabled. Follow-ups: - Add dashboard panels + alert thresholds in observability-pack (tracked in ENG-2201). - Wire these metrics into the Dedicated overload mitigation runbook guidance once alerting is proven in production.
commits: runtime/scheduler: add queue depth gauge and queue wait histogram
runtime/scheduler: export active_requests + batch_size metrics at dispatch
runtime/telemetry: implement rolling EWMA for effective output tokens/sec
runtime/tracing: add spans for enqueue/dispatch and runtime prefill/decode phases
tests: add metric emission unit tests + scheduler overhead micro-benchmark
docs: brief note on labels/cardinality + config flags
review_conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can you clarify how effective_output_tokens_per_second is computed? We should avoid double-smoothing (EWMA + PromQL rate) and make sure it’s deterministic across restarts. Also, queue_depth should be sampled at enqueue and dispatch—what’s the intended interpretation? Sofia Ivanova (author): Added a design note in the PR description + comments: the gauge is process-local EWMA over the counter delta with 30s half-life; it resets on restart (expected) but counters remain monotonic for long-range queries. Dashboards can use either, but the gauge is intended for consistent panels/alerts without relying on query windows. Queue_depth gauge is instantaneous depth; queue_depth_at_dispatch is emitted as histogram observation on dispatch for correlation with batch_size and wait time. Logan Wright (review): Label set includes deployment_id; are we confident about cardinality? In shared clusters, this will explode. Also, please ensure model label is normalized and not raw model_name from request. Sofia Ivanova (author): Added config guardrail: DEPLOYMENT_ID_METRICS_LABEL_ENABLED defaults false for shared/hosted; Dedicated configs will enable. Model label now uses catalog slug (or "unknown") and is capped to a fixed allowlist from the model registry. Removed request-provided model_name from labels entirely. Aisha Bello (review): Histogram buckets for queue_wait_ms look too fine-grained at the high end; for SLO triage we care about 10ms–10s. Also, make sure the tracing spans won’t page oncall by increasing ingest cost unexpectedly. Sofia Ivanova (author): Updated buckets to [1, 2.5, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000]ms and added sampling: tracing spans for prefill/decode are always created but only annotated with token counts when duration > 2ms to reduce attribute churn; overall trace sampling remains controlled by existing sampler config. Sergio Costa (review): Please align metric names with dashboard conventions (redwood_runtime_*), and add one example query snippet to docs so dashboard work is straightforward. Sofia Ivanova (author): Renamed all scheduler metrics under redwood_runtime_scheduler_* and added example PromQL + Grafana panel notes to docs/observability/runtime-metrics.md. Noah Patel (final): Looks good after the label + bucket updates. Approved. Logan Wright (final): Approved with the deployment_id gating; thanks for the normalization changes. Aisha Bello (final): Approved; please ensure rollout is staged for Dedicated first. Merged via squash.
